One row per vendor account. If the same vendor shows up twice (two issues, two names), it's one row under the name on its invoice, and the newer issue is the duplicate.\\n2. Leave out people, contractors and professional firms (legal, accounting, Sunset), taxes and filing services, insurance, bank fees, one-off purchases, anything the company itself never paid for, and anything cancelled before Feb 9. Exception: anything on Sunset's list goes on the register whatever else applies.\\n3. Arthur's project came from the P&L and our lists; he skipped one-off, filing and insurance lines and ones long gone. AWS and the ad accounts in the UA line stay off the register: he and I are closing those out ourselves. Before you call it complete, add what it misses inside any other costs-tab line that covers several vendors \\u2014 each account there gets its own row.\\n4. What we do: Cancel, Keep (my keep list, as amended in the thread), Move to Arthur's LLC (his card), or Hold for Sunset. Sunset's list wins over everything above.\\n5. Where it stands, for Cancel rows only: Closed = the vendor itself has confirmed (their email, an in-app or bot notice, a final invoice) \\u2014 say where. Requested = one of us has cancelled or asked but nothing has come back from the vendor. Open = nobody has done anything yet. Leave it blank on the other rows.\\n6. By when: for Cancel rows that aren't Closed, the day before the next charge (for accounts billed on usage \\u2014 ads, cloud \\u2014 use Feb 28), or the SVB card on the founders' board if it sets an earlier date. For Keep and Hold rows still charging the SVB card while we need them, follow SVB's card terms. Hold rows already off that card, or that won't charge it again before Sunset's review call, stay until the review call; Keep rows that aren't on the SVB card get a dash. Moved and Closed rows get a dash, unless an export or a switch-over still has to happen before the access ends \\u2014 then the day before it ends.\\n7. Owner: the Linear assignee unless the issue hands it to someone else. Anything you add is yours.\\n8. Monthly cost, rounded to cents: the monthly figure its owner gives in its Linear issue, or else its own last invoice or receipt brought to a month (annual \\u00f7 12, quarterly \\u00f7 3). Free plans and accounts that have never charged us are 0.\\n9. Two totals at the bottom: the sum of the monthly cost column over every row (what it all costs us today), and the same sum over the Keep and Hold rows only (what's left after the plan).\\n10. A clash is a decision one of us already posted in #winddown that Sunset's list or SVB's card terms would undo. Moving who pays for an account isn't one (it closes nothing), and requests or suggestions aren't decisions.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_1326e66bcabfda8fd29e4a", "title": "Close-out register conventions", "name": "Close-out register conventions", "revisionId": "8b9413d402", "createdTime": "2026-02-13T16:38:02Z", "modifiedTime": "2026-02-13T16:58:40Z", "text": "Close-out register conventions
1. One row per vendor account. If the same vendor shows up twice (two issues, two names), it's one row under the name on its invoice, and the newer issue is the duplicate.
2. Leave out people, contractors and professional firms (legal, accounting, Sunset), taxes and filing services, insurance, bank fees, one-off purchases, anything the company itself never paid for, and anything cancelled before Feb 9. Exception: anything on Sunset's list goes on the register whatever else applies.
3. Arthur's project came from the P&L and our lists; he skipped one-off, filing and insurance lines and ones long gone. AWS and the ad accounts in the UA line stay off the register: he and I are closing those out ourselves. Before you call it complete, add what it misses inside any other costs-tab line that covers several vendors — each account there gets its own row.
4. What we do: Cancel, Keep (my keep list, as amended in the thread), Move to Arthur's LLC (his card), or Hold for Sunset. Sunset's list wins over everything above.
5. Where it stands, for Cancel rows only: Closed = the vendor itself has confirmed (their email, an in-app or bot notice, a final invoice) — say where. Requested = one of us has cancelled or asked but nothing has come back from the vendor. Open = nobody has done anything yet. Leave it blank on the other rows.
6. By when: for Cancel rows that aren't Closed, the day before the next charge (for accounts billed on usage — ads, cloud — use Feb 28), or the SVB card on the founders' board if it sets an earlier date. For Keep and Hold rows still charging the SVB card while we need them, follow SVB's card terms. Hold rows already off that card, or that won't charge it again before Sunset's review call, stay until the review call; Keep rows that aren't on the SVB card get a dash. Moved and Closed rows get a dash, unless an export or a switch-over still has to happen before the access ends — then the day before it ends.
7. Owner: the Linear assignee unless the issue hands it to someone else. Anything you add is yours.
8. Monthly cost, rounded to cents: the monthly figure its owner gives in its Linear issue, or else its own last invoice or receipt brought to a month (annual ÷ 12, quarterly ÷ 3). Free plans and accounts that have never charged us are 0.
9. Two totals at the bottom: the sum of the monthly cost column over every row (what it all costs us today), and the same sum over the Keep and Hold rows only (what's left after the plan).
10. A clash is a decision one of us already posted in #winddown that Sunset's list or SVB's card terms would undo. Moving who pays for an account isn't one (it closes nothing), and requests or suggestions aren't decisions.
"}

Hi Leonard, Robert, Arthur,

Thanks for signing today. Before we can deliver the licensed data set, these accounts need to stay active with their full history and every user in place until we confirm delivery: Slack (stay on the paid plan — the free plan hides history older than 90 days), Google Workspace (every user account, including former staff — please don't archive or delete any), Figma, Linear, GitHub and Metabase. Nothing on this list should be closed, downgraded or archived before the delivery review call Leonard booked with us. Accounts that aren't on the list aren't part of the licensed bundle, so close them whenever suits you.

For Helpshift, please export the full ticket history to Drive before your subscription ends.

If our engineers change anything on this list, we'll reply on this thread.

Best,
Maya
Client onboarding, Sunset
=====

Maya
=====
Leonard,

As promised on our call, here is the checklist we run on an assignment for the benefit of creditors:
1. Cancel every subscription right away except payroll and accounting.
2. Export whatever records you need before you cancel.
3. Close the company cards last, once nothing bills them.

If you decide to engage us we would run this for you.

Best,
Sherwood Partners
=====

I’m writing to share a difficult update: we have decided to wind down harmonygames.

Despite multiple iterations, we did not get the metrics to a point that supports a viable business path, and we do not have the funding to continue operating while searching for a new direction.
What we did and what we learned
• We built and tested three games on a limited budget, staying true to our mission of hybridcasual gameplay with RPG depth.
• We took real creative risks and pushed to innovate:
Domino Delights: Domino/Tripeak solitaire gameplay with RPG elements
Zombie Match 3D: Match Factory style core loop with RPG combat/progression elements
Combo Fighter: Tetris-like block gameplay with RPG elements
• We also explored partnerships and other paths to scale distribution and improve outcomes, but none changed the trajectory enough.
Financial context
• We have been in sustained financial hardship since mid-2025.
• Revenue did not reach meaningful levels, and the plans we pursued to change that did not work.
• Given our current runway of less than a month and obligations, continuing would create risk without a responsible probability of success.
What happens next
• We are initiating an orderly wind-down process and preparing the required board resolutions and documentation.
• Our priorities are to handle employee and contractor obligations properly, meet tax and compliance requirements, close out vendor commitments, and Sunset the products in a controlled way.
• We will also evaluate what to do with the remaining IP and codebase (archive, sale, or other disposition) and will keep you informed.
Timeline and updates
• We will share a more detailed wind-down plan and timeline shortly, including key dates for operational shutdown.
• I will send periodic updates as we complete the major steps and once we have clarity on final liabilities and any remaining assets.
I regret having to send this. I am proud of the team we put together and the quality of what we shipped. We ran a frugal operation, made multiple bets, and pushed hard, but we did not reach the performance required to build a durable company.

• Game has no IAP still", "channel": "C09UHHN6PFZ", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID", "thread_ts": "1770059391.060159"}, {"ts": "1770058974.897419", "type": "message", "text": "Recap, this is what we're doing:

The idea is that we will assign a user to a different level list that will give us different levels.", "channel": "C09UHHN6PFZ", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID"}, {"ts": "1769910590.802789", "type": "message", "text": "I think I just created a new player and didn't get it either", "channel": "C09UHHN6PFZ", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0025_SLACK_ID"}, {"ts": "1769892773.615929", "type": "message", "text": "I like the idea of applying a multiplier based on how far a player’s upgrades are above or below the expected upgrade to address “ahead early, stays ahead for 10+ levels.”", "channel": "C09UHHN6PFZ", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID", "thread_ts": "1769885600.421359"}, {"ts": "1769892718.932069", "type": "message", "text": "Simple improvement: Upgrade-adjusted difficulty multiplier (plus a tiny “skill” correction)
Keep your current per-level curve, but apply a multiplier based on how far a player’s upgrades are above or below the expected upgrade curve for that level. This directly addresses “ahead early, stays ahead for 10+ levels.”
1) Compute an upgrade power score
Use what you already have (HP, Regen, Attack upgrades). Start linear.
• `U = 0.4 * HP + 0.3 * Regen + 0.3 * Attack`
(Adjust weights later if Attack dominates outcomes, but start here.)
2) Maintain an expected upgrade curve by level
You need `E[level] = expected U at this level` from either:
design intent (a table), or
• median `U` from live data per level (better once you have enough data).
3) Convert “ahead/behind” into a difficulty multiplier
• `delta = U - E[level]`
• `M_upg = clamp(1 + k * delta, 0.85, 1.25)`
Where `k` is small (start `k = 0.05`).
Example using your comment “3 to 4 levels ahead”: if that maps to `delta = +2`, then `M_upg = 1.10`. That is enough to pull you back into “need to think” without nuking average players.
4) Optional, still simple: a 3-bucket “skill” correction
This keeps the fully-upgraded-but-crappy player from getting obliterated instantly, while still letting them struggle.
Define `S` from the last 3 to 5 levels using only cheap telemetry:
• attempts per level
• time to clear
• waves reached at death (if you have it)
• number of refreshes (if relevant)
Bucket it:
• *Strong*: low attempts, fast clears
• *Average*: middle
• *Weak*: high attempts, slow clears
Then:
• `M_skill = {Strong: 1.05, Average: 1.00, Weak: 0.95}`
Final:
• `M = M_upg * M_skill` (still clamped to 0.85 to 1.25)
5) Apply M to a small set of knobs only
Do not touch everything. Pick 2 to 3 levers that reliably create “I have to rebuild now” moments.
Good candidates:
• enemy HP (or base health pool per wave)
• enemy damage (or time-to-death pressure)
• obstacle density or obstacle removal cost
• shape pool entropy (only if it is a main difficulty driver, and you can change it safely)
Example:
• `EnemyHP = BaseEnemyHP(level, wave) * M`
• `EnemyDPS = BaseEnemyDPS(level, wave) * (0.5 + 0.5*M)`
(less aggressive than HP if DPS spikes feel unfair)
A/B test design
*Control (A)*: current level-based curve.
*Variant (B)*: same curve times `M` (upgrade-adjusted, plus optional skill bucket).
Primary success criteria (pick 2 to avoid overfitting):
• level completion rate and attempts distribution (especially levels 10 to 25)
• time per level and “rebuild events” frequency proxy (big board changes, silver spend spikes, obstacle removals)
• D1 and D3 retention (segmented by payer vs non-payer, and by upgrade delta buckets)
Key segmentation to validate the exact argument in your thread:
• `delta >= +2` (ahead of curve, your “spender/optimizer” proxy)
• `delta between -1 and +1` (on-curve average)
• `delta <= -2` (behind curve)
Expected outcome if this works:
• ahead-of-curve players stop cruising for 10 levels, they hit meaningful rebuilds earlier (around level 11 to 12 if that’s your target)
• average players stay near current difficulty
• weak players still struggle, but not catastrophically earlier than today (your existing retry-based adjustments can remain as the safety net)
If you want the minimum possible engineering change: implement only `M_upg` with a clamped multiplier, apply it to enemy HP only, ship the A/B. That alone will tell you if upgrade variance is the real driver.", "channel": "C09UHHN6PFZ", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID", "thread_ts": "1769885600.421359"}, {"ts": "1769892530.230299", "type": "message", "text": "half of players get the current level difficulty curve, the other half gets upgrade-adjusted difficulty curve and then we compare", "channel": "C09UHHN6PFZ", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID", "thread_ts": "1769885600.421359"}], "has_more": true, "total_count": 6120, "response_metadata": {"next_cursor": "c2VhcmNoOm09MTc2OTg5MjUzMC4yMzAyOTklN0MzYjFhMDY3ZDE4OGEyODc4YWM0NTgwMmZlZDU3NjVmODtkPWQ7cz1hbGw="}}

What the contract actually does (plain summary)\\n*Parties and scope*\\n\\u2022 Between MAXFLOW BV (CrazyGames) as Publisher and Harmony Games as Partner.\\n\\u2022 Covers Domino Delights and Zombie Match 3D.\\n\\u2022 License: world-wide, non-exclusive, _transferable_ license to publish the games on \\u201cLicensed Platforms.\\u201d\\n*Licensed Platforms*\\nDefined very broadly as:\\n\\u2022 <http://CrazyGames.com|CrazyGames.com> and its domains / apps\\n\\u2022 other WebGL or HTML5 browser platforms\\n\\u2022 mobile app stores\\nSo by default this contract covers both web and mobile, not just CrazyGames.\\n*Revenue share*\\n\\u2022 Game Revenue is defined as ad + IAP revenue _after_ deducting: agency commissions, ad serving costs, platform fees, payment processing, and VAT/other taxes.\\n\\u2022 Net amount is then split: 40 % Publisher, 60 % Partner.\\n*Hosting and SDK*\\n\\u2022 Technology is \\u201cPublisher hosting\\u201d for these games, so you give them a full build, they host it.\\n\\u2022 You must integrate their SDK, keep it up to date, and, on request, update SDK to the most recent version up to 1 year _after termination_ or make it possible for them to integrate the SDK into the game themselves.\\n*Game updates and parity*\\nYou must:\\n\\u2022 Deliver the game within 6 months.\\n\\u2022 Keep the web version \\u201calways identical to the latest version\\u201d on your own sites and any other platforms.\\n\\u2022 Ship updates to them no later than anyone else, fix bugs promptly, and provide reasonable ongoing support.\\n*Outbound links and monetization*\\n\\u2022 You cannot include outbound links in the game (for example to your site or app stores) without their explicit written consent.\\n\\u2022 They have the exclusive right to serve ads and IAPs on Licensed Platforms. You can only include IAPs with their approval.\\n*Term, renewal, and transition*\\n\\u2022 Initial term: 1 year starting when the game is released on the Licensed Platforms.\\n\\u2022 Automatic renewal for the same period, unless a party gives 3 months written notice before the end of a term.\\n\\u2022 After expiry or termination, they _may_ keep the game live for a 6-month \\u201cTransition Period\\u201d and you must keep providing services and cooperation during that time.\\n*Termination*\\n\\u2022 Both parties can terminate for material breach, insolvency, etc., with cure periods for some items.\\n\\u2022 Publisher has extra rights to terminate immediately, without liability, if There is alleged IP infringement, breach of warranties, or breach of your obligations.\\n\\u2022 There is _no_ mutual termination for convenience anywhere.\\n*Liability, indemnity, and IP*\\n\\u2022 You give broad warranties that you own all IP, do not infringe, comply with laws, no viruses, high quality, etc.\\n\\u2022 You indemnify them for IP infringements, legal breaches, and any claims about game content, with no explicit cap.\\n\\u2022 Their liability is capped at \\u201cfees paid or payable to Partner under the Agreement\\u201d and they disclaim most warranties for their portal.\\n\\u2022 They can act in your name to issue takedowns against copycats, but have no duty to litigate.\\n*Data and marketing*\\n\\u2022 Each party is an independent controller for personal data, must comply with GDPR etc.\\n\\u2022 You cannot use personal data beyond what is necessary, and cannot promote your own or third-party content on their platforms without their written consent.\\n*Law and venue*\\n\\u2022 Governing law: Belgium.\\n\\u2022 Exclusive courts: Leuven, Belgium.\\n2. Key red flags and items to Push on\\nA. Platform scope: they are grabbing mobile by default\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 Licensed Platforms includes \\u201cmobile app stores,\\u201d and the license is world-wide, transferable, and covers publishing and monetization There.\\n\\u2022 Combined with their exclusive right to serve ads and IAP on Licensed Platforms, this pulls mobile into their control unless you carve it out.\\nPushback / clarification:\\n\\u2022 Restrict the Licensed Platforms to _web only_ for this agreement, for example:\\n    \\u25e6 \\u201cLicensed Platforms: <http://www.CrazyGames.com|www.CrazyGames.com> and other HTML5/WebGL browser game portals. For the avoidance of doubt, this Agreement does not apply to any mobile app store distribution.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Or, if you want to allow some mobile experiment later, create a _separate_ mobile addendum with tight scope and your veto on any mobile publishing.\\nThis aligns with your plan to keep mobile separate and talk to other mobile publishers.\\n\\nB. Transferable license + easy assignment by them\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 License is explicitly \\u201ctransferable.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Assignment clause lets _them_ assign the whole agreement to a third party with only notification, while you cannot assign without their consent.\\nThis means they can sell or spin out your games\\u2019 web rights to another company without your approval.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Make the license non-transferable except to their owned affiliates, or require your prior written consent for any assignment or sublicensing to non-affiliates.\\n\\u2022 Make assignment more symmetric: you can at least assign to an acquirer of Harmony Games without needing their consent.\\nC. Term, auto-renewal, no convenience exit, plus 6-month transition\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 Initial 1-year term, automatic 1-year renewals, and you must give 3 months notice before the term ends to stop renewal.\\n\\u2022 After any end, they can keep the game live for 6 more months, and you must support it.\\n\\u2022 There is no termination for convenience for you at all.\\nIn practice that is a long lockdown. If you miss the 3-month window, you are locked for another year plus up to 6 months of transition.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Add mutual termination for convenience, for example:\\n    \\u25e6 \\u201cAfter the first 3 months from launch, either Party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon 30 days written notice.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Reduce the Transition Period or remove it. If you accept any transition, limit it to 30 days, and clarify that:\\n    \\u25e6 Your support obligation is minimal (no new features, only critical bug fixes).\\n    \\u25e6 They cannot launch the game on new platforms during the transition.\\n\\u2022 If they insist on the 6-month Transition Period, tie it only to expiry of a term, not to early termination for convenience or breach.\\nThis directly reduces the lockdown period you are worried about.\\n\\nD. SDK and support obligations, including after termination\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 You must implement and keep their SDK up to date, and on request update it \\u201cuntil 1 year after termination,\\u201d or else \\u201cmake it possible for Publisher to integrate the SDK within the Game(s) itself.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 You must keep the web version identical to the latest version on all other platforms, deliver updates to them no later than others, quickly fix defects, and answer their questions.\\nRisks:\\n\\u2022 You are on the hook for live-ops style support even when the deal is effectively over.\\n\\u2022 \\u201cMake it possible for Publisher to integrate the SDK\\u201d is vague and could be interpreted as pressure to expose more of your build pipeline or code than you want.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Limit post-termination obligations: for example, \\u201cup to 60 days after termination, best-effort support limited to critical bug fixes, no new SDK integrations.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Clarify that you are not required to provide source code or build scripts and that SDK integration will always be done by you at your discretion.\\n\\u2022 Relax \\u201calways identical\\u201d wording so you can test features on other platforms first or maintain a lighter web build.\\nE. Monetization and outbound links: they control everything\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 They have the exclusive right to serve ads and IAPs within the game on Licensed Platforms.\\n\\u2022 You cannot add Outbound Links or promote your own or third-party content through their platforms without explicit written consent.\\nImpact:\\n\\u2022 You cannot naturally promote your own mobile versions or cross-promote your other games from the web build without their explicit permission.\\n\\u2022 Any IAP system in the web version requires their approval and flows through their billing.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Carve out specific outbound links that are always allowed, for example:\\n    \\u25e6 \\u201cPartner may include links to Partner\\u2019s official website, and to Domino Delights and Zombie Match mobile store pages, subject to Publisher\\u2019s UX requirements, without separate written approval.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Clarify that cross-promotion of your own titles within the game is permitted, provided it does not conflict with their ad inventory.\\n\\u2022 If you ever want to test your own IAP stack on web, you need at least a negotiation clause instead of pure veto.\\nF. Indemnities and liability are very one-sided\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 Your indemnity is broad and uncapped in the text: IP infringement, data protection, any claims about content, plus breach of warranties.\\n\\u2022 Their total liability is capped at \\u201cthe fees paid or payable to Partner,\\u201d and they generally disclaim warranties for their site.\\nThis means:\\n\\u2022 Worst-case legal risks related to content, data, or IP are largely on you, while their downside is effectively limited to what they have already paid you.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Add a reciprocal indemnity from them covering:\\n    \\u25e6 Their SDK, ad tech, tracking, and any UA / ad network practices on their side.\\n    \\u25e6 Infringement by their branding or assets, and violations of data protection laws arising from their processing.\\n\\u2022 Introduce caps and carve-outs:\\n    \\u25e6 Cap your indemnity and their liability at a defined multiple of annual fees, with higher caps only for IP or data breaches if needed.\\n\\u2022 Tighten the IP warranties so you are not giving absolute guarantees far beyond what is realistic.\\nG. Right of first refusal on variations (sequels etc.)\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 The exclusivity clause says that where There is an exclusive game, Publisher has a right of first refusal on variations (sequels, prequels, etc.) under the same terms and conditions.\\nIn this specific Game Order the license is \\u201cnon-exclusive,\\u201d so this clause should not bite now, but it is still sitting There.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Explicitly state in the main agreement or Game Order that:\\n    \\u25e6 \\u201cThe exclusivity provisions and right of first refusal in Annex 2, Article 8 do not apply to this Agreement or to any variations of the Games unless explicitly agreed in a future Game Order.\\u201d\\nThis prevents later arguments that you owe them first dibs on sequels.\\n\\nH. Self-billing, reporting, and audit\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 They issue self-billing invoices and if you do not object within a short time window, they are deemed accepted.\\n\\u2022 Strong offset rights if ad networks fail to pay them.\\n\\u2022 No explicit reporting detail or audit rights are spelled out.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Ask for:\\n    \\u25e6 Monthly detailed revenue reports by platform, geography, ad network, and ad/IAP split.\\n    \\u25e6 A clear dispute window of at least 30 days from receipt of a statement, with a defined process.\\n    \\u25e6 A right to audit or have a third-party auditor review their numbers once per year at your cost if discrepancies above a threshold are found.\\nI. Governing law and venue\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 Belgium law, courts of Leuven for any disputes.\\nIf you can live with that, you leave it. If you want less friction:\\n\\u2022 Propose arbitration in a neutral venue or at least a less one-sided forum clause.\\n\\u2022 At minimum, you can leave this as \\u201cnot a hill to die on\\u201d if your main concern is web scope and lock-in, but be aware of the litigation friction.\\n3. Priority list given your goals\\nGiven what you said you care about (web only, shorter lockdown, easy exit, control if they disappoint), I would prioritize:\\n1. *Scope and platforms*: Remove \\u201cmobile app stores\\u201d from Licensed Platforms and make this a pure web publishing deal.\\n2. *Term and exit*: Add mutual termination for convenience with 30 days notice after an initial test period, and shorten or heavily constrain the 6-month Transition Period.\\n3. *Transferability / assignment*: Remove transferability beyond affiliates and require your consent for assignments.\\n4. *Monetization and links*: Explicit rights to link to and promote your own mobile versions and titles, within clear UX bounds.\\n5. *Indemnity balance*: Add mutual SDK / UA indemnity, cap your exposure, and fix the asymmetry.\\n6. *Support tail*: Limit SDK and support obligations after termination.\\nIf you paste your current redline or the email you are sending back, I can rewrite it to focus precisely on these points so There is no ambiguity.\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1763421013.739279\"}, {\"ts\": \"1751041721.856569\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"another person abusing us not checking the receipts I think <@EMPLOYEE_0025_SLACK_ID> <https://harmonygames.metabaseapp.com/question#eyJuYW1lIjoiSUFQIFJldmVudWUgYnkgRGF5IiwiZGVzY3JpcHRpb24iOm51bGwsImRhdGFzZXRfcXVlcnkiOnsiZGF0YWJhc2UiOjIsInF1ZXJ5Ijp7ImZpbHRlciI6WyJhbmQiLFsiPSIsWyJmaWVsZCIsMzQ0OCx7ImJhc2UtdHlwZSI6InR5cGUvRGF0ZVRpbWVXaXRoTG9jYWxUWiIsInRlbXBvcmFsLXVuaXQiOiJkYXkifV0sIjIwMjUtMDYtMjZUMDA6MDA6MDBaIl0sWyI-|https://harmonygames.metabaseapp.com/question#eyJuYW1lIjoiSUFQIFJldmVudWUgYnkgRGF5IiwiZGVzY3Jpc[\\u2026]5hbF9jYXJkX2lkIjpudWxsLCJ0eXBlIjoicXVlc3Rpb24ifQ==>\", \"channel\": \"C080X4GTZ0E\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1748583702.550559\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"\\u2022 :[USERNAME_22310]: ----- Art Department - What the contract actually does (plain summary)\\n*Parties and scope*\\n\\u2022 Between MAXFLOW BV (CrazyGames) as Publisher and Harmony Games as Partner.\\n\\u2022 Covers Domino Delights and Zombie Match 3D.\\n\\u2022 License: world-wide, non-exclusive, _transferable_ license to publish the games on \\u201cLicensed Platforms.\\u201d\\n*Licensed Platforms*\\nDefined very broadly as:\\n\\u2022 <http://CrazyGames.com|CrazyGames.com> and its domains / apps\\n\\u2022 other WebGL or HTML5 browser platforms\\n\\u2022 mobile app stores\\nSo by default this contract covers both web and mobile, not just CrazyGames.\\n*Revenue share*\\n\\u2022 Game Revenue is defined as ad + IAP revenue _after_ deducting: agency commissions, ad serving costs, platform fees, payment processing, and VAT/other taxes.\\n\\u2022 Net amount is then split: 40 % Publisher, 60 % Partner.\\n*Hosting and SDK*\\n\\u2022 Technology is \\u201cPublisher hosting\\u201d for these games, so you give them a full build, they host it.\\n\\u2022 You must integrate their SDK, keep it up to date, and, on request, update SDK to the most recent version up to 1 year _after termination_ or make it possible for them to integrate the SDK into the game themselves.\\n*Game updates and parity*\\nYou must:\\n\\u2022 Deliver the game within 6 months.\\n\\u2022 Keep the web version \\u201calways identical to the latest version\\u201d on your own sites and any other platforms.\\n\\u2022 Ship updates to them no later than anyone else, fix bugs promptly, and provide reasonable ongoing support.\\n*Outbound links and monetization*\\n\\u2022 You cannot include outbound links in the game (for example to your site or app stores) without their explicit written consent.\\n\\u2022 They have the exclusive right to serve ads and IAPs on Licensed Platforms. You can only include IAPs with their approval.\\n*Term, renewal, and transition*\\n\\u2022 Initial term: 1 year starting when the game is released on the Licensed Platforms.\\n\\u2022 Automatic renewal for the same period, unless a party gives 3 months written notice before the end of a term.\\n\\u2022 After expiry or termination, they _may_ keep the game live for a 6-month \\u201cTransition Period\\u201d and you must keep providing services and cooperation during that time.\\n*Termination*\\n\\u2022 Both parties can terminate for material breach, insolvency, etc., with cure periods for some items.\\n\\u2022 Publisher has extra rights to terminate immediately, without liability, if There is alleged IP infringement, breach of warranties, or breach of your obligations.\\n\\u2022 There is _no_ mutual termination for convenience anywhere.\\n*Liability, indemnity, and IP*\\n\\u2022 You give broad warranties that you own all IP, do not infringe, comply with laws, no viruses, high quality, etc.\\n\\u2022 You indemnify them for IP infringements, legal breaches, and any claims about game content, with no explicit cap.\\n\\u2022 Their liability is capped at \\u201cfees paid or payable to Partner under the Agreement\\u201d and they disclaim most warranties for their portal.\\n\\u2022 They can act in your name to issue takedowns against copycats, but have no duty to litigate.\\n*Data and marketing*\\n\\u2022 Each party is an independent controller for personal data, must comply with GDPR etc.\\n\\u2022 You cannot use personal data beyond what is necessary, and cannot promote your own or third-party content on their platforms without their written consent.\\n*Law and venue*\\n\\u2022 Governing law: Belgium.\\n\\u2022 Exclusive courts: Leuven, Belgium.\\n2. Key red flags and items to Push on\\nA. Platform scope: they are grabbing mobile by default\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 Licensed Platforms includes \\u201cmobile app stores,\\u201d and the license is world-wide, transferable, and covers publishing and monetization There.\\n\\u2022 Combined with their exclusive right to serve ads and IAP on Licensed Platforms, this pulls mobile into their control unless you carve it out.\\nPushback / clarification:\\n\\u2022 Restrict the Licensed Platforms to _web only_ for this agreement, for example:\\n    \\u25e6 \\u201cLicensed Platforms: <http://www.CrazyGames.com|www.CrazyGames.com> and other HTML5/WebGL browser game portals. For the avoidance of doubt, this Agreement does not apply to any mobile app store distribution.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Or, if you want to allow some mobile experiment later, create a _separate_ mobile addendum with tight scope and your veto on any mobile publishing.\\nThis aligns with your plan to keep mobile separate and talk to other mobile publishers.\\n\\nB. Transferable license + easy assignment by them\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 License is explicitly \\u201ctransferable.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Assignment clause lets _them_ assign the whole agreement to a third party with only notification, while you cannot assign without their consent.\\nThis means they can sell or spin out your games\\u2019 web rights to another company without your approval.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Make the license non-transferable except to their owned affiliates, or require your prior written consent for any assignment or sublicensing to non-affiliates.\\n\\u2022 Make assignment more symmetric: you can at least assign to an acquirer of Harmony Games without needing their consent.\\nC. Term, auto-renewal, no convenience exit, plus 6-month transition\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 Initial 1-year term, automatic 1-year renewals, and you must give 3 months notice before the term ends to stop renewal.\\n\\u2022 After any end, they can keep the game live for 6 more months, and you must support it.\\n\\u2022 There is no termination for convenience for you at all.\\nIn practice that is a long lockdown. If you miss the 3-month window, you are locked for another year plus up to 6 months of transition.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Add mutual termination for convenience, for example:\\n    \\u25e6 \\u201cAfter the first 3 months from launch, either Party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon 30 days written notice.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Reduce the Transition Period or remove it. If you accept any transition, limit it to 30 days, and clarify that:\\n    \\u25e6 Your support obligation is minimal (no new features, only critical bug fixes).\\n    \\u25e6 They cannot launch the game on new platforms during the transition.\\n\\u2022 If they insist on the 6-month Transition Period, tie it only to expiry of a term, not to early termination for convenience or breach.\\nThis directly reduces the lockdown period you are worried about.\\n\\nD. SDK and support obligations, including after termination\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 You must implement and keep their SDK up to date, and on request update it \\u201cuntil 1 year after termination,\\u201d or else \\u201cmake it possible for Publisher to integrate the SDK within the Game(s) itself.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 You must keep the web version identical to the latest version on all other platforms, deliver updates to them no later than others, quickly fix defects, and answer their questions.\\nRisks:\\n\\u2022 You are on the hook for live-ops style support even when the deal is effectively over.\\n\\u2022 \\u201cMake it possible for Publisher to integrate the SDK\\u201d is vague and could be interpreted as pressure to expose more of your build pipeline or code than you want.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Limit post-termination obligations: for example, \\u201cup to 60 days after termination, best-effort support limited to critical bug fixes, no new SDK integrations.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Clarify that you are not required to provide source code or build scripts and that SDK integration will always be done by you at your discretion.\\n\\u2022 Relax \\u201calways identical\\u201d wording so you can test features on other platforms first or maintain a lighter web build.\\nE. {"ok": true, "messages": [{"ts": "1763421018.863089", "type": "message", "text": "Here is the structure of the deal and where I would Push back.

1. What the contract actually does (plain summary)
*Parties and scope*
• Between MAXFLOW BV (CrazyGames) as Publisher and Harmony Games as Partner.
• Covers Domino Delights and Zombie Match 3D.
• License: world-wide, non-exclusive, _transferable_ license to publish the games on “Licensed Platforms.”
*Licensed Platforms*
Defined very broadly as:
• <http://CrazyGames.com|CrazyGames.com> and its domains / apps
• other WebGL or HTML5 browser platforms
• mobile app stores
So by default this contract covers both web and mobile, not just CrazyGames.
*Revenue share*
• Game Revenue is defined as ad + IAP revenue _after_ deducting: agency commissions, ad serving costs, platform fees, payment processing, and VAT/other taxes.
• Net amount is then split: 40 % Publisher, 60 % Partner.
*Hosting and SDK*
• Technology is “Publisher hosting” for these games, so you give them a full build, they host it.
• You must integrate their SDK, keep it up to date, and, on request, update SDK to the most recent version up to 1 year _after termination_ or make it possible for them to integrate the SDK into the game themselves.
*Game updates and parity*
You must:
• Deliver the game within 6 months.
• Keep the web version “always identical to the latest version” on your own sites and any other platforms.
• Ship updates to them no later than anyone else, fix bugs promptly, and provide reasonable ongoing support.
*Outbound links and monetization*
• You cannot include outbound links in the game (for example to your site or app stores) without their explicit written consent.
• They have the exclusive right to serve ads and IAPs on Licensed Platforms. You can only include IAPs with their approval.
*Term, renewal, and transition*
• Initial term: 1 year starting when the game is released on the Licensed Platforms.
• Automatic renewal for the same period, unless a party gives 3 months written notice before the end of a term.
• After expiry or termination, they _may_ keep the game live for a 6-month “Transition Period” and you must keep providing services and cooperation during that time.
*Termination*
• Both parties can terminate for material breach, insolvency, etc., with cure periods for some items.
• Publisher has extra rights to terminate immediately, without liability, if There is alleged IP infringement, breach of warranties, or breach of your obligations.
• There is _no_ mutual termination for convenience anywhere.
*Liability, indemnity, and IP*
• You give broad warranties that you own all IP, do not infringe, comply with laws, no viruses, high quality, etc.
• You indemnify them for IP infringements, legal breaches, and any claims about game content, with no explicit cap.
• Their liability is capped at “fees paid or payable to Partner under the Agreement” and they disclaim most warranties for their portal.
• They can act in your name to issue takedowns against copycats, but have no duty to litigate.
*Data and marketing*
• Each party is an independent controller for personal data, must comply with GDPR etc.
• You cannot use personal data beyond what is necessary, and cannot promote your own or third-party content on their platforms without their written consent.
*Law and venue*
• Governing law: Belgium.
• Exclusive courts: Leuven, Belgium.
2. Key red flags and items to Push on
A. Platform scope: they are grabbing mobile by default
Problem:
• Licensed Platforms includes “mobile app stores,” and the license is world-wide, transferable, and covers publishing and monetization There.
• Combined with their exclusive right to serve ads and IAP on Licensed Platforms, this pulls mobile into their control unless you carve it out.
Pushback / clarification:
• Restrict the Licensed Platforms to _web only_ for this agreement, for example:
    ◦ “Licensed Platforms: <http://www.CrazyGames.com|www.CrazyGames.com> and other HTML5/WebGL browser game portals. For the avoidance of doubt, this Agreement does not apply to any mobile app store distribution.”
• Or, if you want to allow some mobile experiment later, create a _separate_ mobile addendum with tight scope and your veto on any mobile publishing.
This aligns with your plan to keep mobile separate and talk to other mobile publishers.

B. Transferable license + easy assignment by them
Problem:
• License is explicitly “transferable.”
• Assignment clause lets _them_ assign the whole agreement to a third party with only notification, while you cannot assign without their consent.
This means they can sell or spin out your games’ web rights to another company without your approval.
Pushback:
• Make the license non-transferable except to their owned affiliates, or require your prior written consent for any assignment or sublicensing to non-affiliates.
• Make assignment more symmetric: you can at least assign to an acquirer of Harmony Games without needing their consent.
C. Term, auto-renewal, no convenience exit, plus 6-month transition
Problem:
• Initial 1-year term, automatic 1-year renewals, and you must give 3 months notice before the term ends to stop renewal.
• After any end, they can keep the game live for 6 more months, and you must support it.
• There is no termination for convenience for you at all.
In practice that is a long lockdown. If you miss the 3-month window, you are locked for another year plus up to 6 months of transition.
Pushback:
• Add mutual termination for convenience, for example:
    ◦ “After the first 3 months from launch, either Party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon 30 days written notice.”
• Reduce the Transition Period or remove it. If you accept any transition, limit it to 30 days, and clarify that:
    ◦ Your support obligation is minimal (no new features, only critical bug fixes).
    ◦ They cannot launch the game on new platforms during the transition.
• If they insist on the 6-month Transition Period, tie it only to expiry of a term, not to early termination for convenience or breach.
This directly reduces the lockdown period you are worried about.

D. SDK and support obligations, including after termination
Problem:
• You must implement and keep their SDK up to date, and on request update it “until 1 year after termination,” or else “make it possible for Publisher to integrate the SDK within the Game(s) itself.”
• You must keep the web version identical to the latest version on all other platforms, deliver updates to them no later than others, quickly fix defects, and answer their questions.
Risks:
• You are on the hook for live-ops style support even when the deal is effectively over.
• “Make it possible for Publisher to integrate the SDK” is vague and could be interpreted as pressure to expose more of your build pipeline or code than you want.
Pushback:
• Limit post-termination obligations: for example, “up to 60 days after termination, best-effort support limited to critical bug fixes, no new SDK integrations.”
• Clarify that you are not required to provide source code or build scripts and that SDK integration will always be done by you at your discretion.
• Relax “always identical” wording so you can test features on other platforms first or maintain a lighter web build.
E. Monetization and outbound links: they control everything
Problem:
• They have the exclusive right to serve ads and IAPs within the game on Licensed Platforms.
• You cannot add Outbound Links or promote your own or third-party content through their platforms without explicit written consent.
Impact:
• You cannot naturally promote your own mobile versions or cross-promote your other games from the web build without their explicit permission.
• Any IAP system in the web version requires their approval and flows through their billing.
Pushback:
• Carve out specific outbound links that are always allowed, for example:
    ◦ “Partner may include links to Partner’s official website, and to Domino Delights and Zombie Match mobile store pages, subject to Publisher’s UX requirements, without separate written approval.”
• Clarify that cross-promotion of your own titles within the game is permitted, provided it does not conflict with their ad inventory.
• If you ever want to test your own IAP stack on web, you need at least a negotiation clause instead of pure veto.
F. Indemnities and liability are very one-sided
Problem:
• Your indemnity is broad and uncapped in the text: IP infringement, data protection, any claims about content, plus breach of warranties.
• Their total liability is capped at “the fees paid or payable to Partner,” and they generally disclaim warranties for their site.
This means:
• Worst-case legal risks related to content, data, or IP are largely on you, while their downside is effectively limited to what they have already paid you.
Pushback:
• Add a reciprocal indemnity from them covering:
    ◦ Their SDK, ad tech, tracking, and any UA / ad network practices on their side.
    ◦ Infringement by their branding or assets, and violations of data protection laws arising from their processing.
• Introduce caps and carve-outs:
    ◦ Cap your indemnity and their liability at a defined multiple of annual fees, with higher caps only for IP or data breaches if needed.
• Tighten the IP warranties so you are not giving absolute guarantees far beyond what is realistic.
G. Right of first refusal on variations (sequels etc.)
Problem:
• The exclusivity clause says that where There is an exclusive game, Publisher has a right of first refusal on variations (sequels, prequels, etc.) under the same terms and conditions.
In this specific Game Order the license is “non-exclusive,” so this clause should not bite now, but it is still sitting There.
Pushback:
• Explicitly state in the main agreement or Game Order that:
    ◦ “The exclusivity provisions and right of first refusal in Annex 2, Article 8 do not apply to this Agreement or to any variations of the Games unless explicitly agreed in a future Game Order.”
This prevents later arguments that you owe them first dibs on sequels.

H. Self-billing, reporting, and audit
Problem:
• They issue self-billing invoices and if you do not object within a short time window, they are deemed accepted.
• Strong offset rights if ad networks fail to pay them.
• No explicit reporting detail or audit rights are spelled out.
Pushback:
• Ask for:
    ◦ Monthly detailed revenue reports by platform, geography, ad network, and ad/IAP split.
    ◦ A clear dispute window of at least 30 days from receipt of a statement, with a defined process.
    ◦ A right to audit or have a third-party auditor review their numbers once per year at your cost if discrepancies above a threshold are found.
I. Governing law and venue
Problem:
• Belgium law, courts of Leuven for any disputes.
If you can live with that, you leave it. If you want less friction:
• Propose arbitration in a neutral venue or at least a less one-sided forum clause.
• At minimum, you can leave this as “not a hill to die on” if your main concern is web scope and lock-in, but be aware of the litigation friction.
3. Priority list given your goals
Given what you said you care about (web only, shorter lockdown, easy exit, control if they disappoint), I would prioritize:
1. *Scope and platforms*: Remove “mobile app stores” from Licensed Platforms and make this a pure web publishing deal.
2. *Term and exit*: Add mutual termination for convenience with 30 days notice after an initial test period, and shorten or heavily constrain the 6-month Transition Period.
3. *Transferability / assignment*: Remove transferability beyond affiliates and require your consent for assignments.
4. *Monetization and links*: Explicit rights to link to and promote your own mobile versions and titles, within clear UX bounds.
5. *Indemnity balance*: Add mutual SDK / UA indemnity, cap your exposure, and fix the asymmetry.
6. *Support tail*: Limit SDK and support obligations after termination.

• Everything on the register, i.e. what it all costs us today: **$6,706.49/mo**

• *Google archive after Feb 15* (your Feb 12 list): Sunset's checklist says every Workspace user, former staff included, stays as is, with nothing archived or deleted before the Mar 12 delivery review call. • Not a clash, just worth checking: if the Feb 11 plan to switch Slack to 3 paid seats and make everyone else guests already happened, check it against Sunset's "paid plan, every user in place, full history" before Mar 12.

• QuickBooks/Intuit is one row (Keep), and it has to move off the SVB card by Feb 17. Slack and Workspace have the same deadline.
• I added ElevenLabs, which was buried in the costs-tab "Sound" line ($50/yr, Cancel, mine). Pond5 is already gone.

**Linear**
• Every issue has a comment.
• Done: Helpshift, Zapier, Cursor, Kapwing, Soundly.
• Canceled: Intuit (duplicate of QuickBooks), iPostal (closed Jan 16), Lucidchart (gone since Nov), Google Ads (UA line, yours to close).
• Everything else stays open. Still waiting on vendor confirmation: Unity, Singular, Layer, CodeRabbit.

content.text:
I've built the register, shared it with Leonard and Arthur as editors, settled and commented on all 28 Linear issues, and replied in Leonard's #winddown thread. I followed the rules in the conventions doc he put in the Wind Down folder.

**Register:** [Account close-out register](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1jmDe7tEablev3nPDTnw4joxXOW-sAlkoEH2zbQEl-SU/edit) has 25 accounts. Each row shows what we do with it, where it stands, by when, who does it, the monthly cost and where each number came from. The Wind Down folder wouldn't accept the file, so it's in your Drive.

**The two monthly totals:**
- **Everything we pay today:** $6,706.49/mo
- **What's left after the plan (accounts we keep or hold for Sunset):** $1,249.04/mo

**Clash with what we already decided:** Leonard's plan to archive Google after Feb 15 conflicts with Sunset's data checklist. Sunset wants every Workspace user, former staff included, left in place until the Mar 12 delivery review call. I also told him to check whether the Feb 11 idea of turning most Slack users into guests went ahead, since Sunset wants every user in place on the paid plan. I listed that as something to check, not a clash.

**Two things that drive the dates:**
- **SVB card:** On the founders' Trello board, Leonard says the card now closes Feb 18, not Feb 20. Anything we keep has to be off it by end of day Feb 17, and every cancellation is due Feb 17. Carta is his one exception and runs to Aug 14.
- **Sunset's list changed on Feb 13:** BigQuery, dbt and Trello were added and Metabase was dropped. Metabase is now just moved to Arthur's LLC card.

**Linear:**
- **Done:** Helpshift, Zapier, Cursor, Kapwing and Soundly. Each vendor confirmed the cancellation.
- **Canceled:** Intuit (same account as QuickBooks), iPostal (already cancelled Jan 16), Lucidchart (expired last November) and Google Ads (an ad account Leonard is closing himself).
- **Still open:** everything else. Unity, Singular, Layer and CodeRabbit have been cancelled or asked to cancel, but the vendors haven't confirmed yet.

**Your items** (dates are end of day):
- **Docusign:** Leonard handed it to you; cancel by Feb 17.
- **ElevenLabs:** I added it because it was hidden inside the costs-tab "Sound" line; it's $50 a year, so cancel by Feb 17.
- **Figma:** holds for Sunset until Mar 12; no charge until it renews in September.
- **Soundly:** already closed.

Gusto, QuickBooks, Slack and Workspace also have Feb 17 deadlines, but those are Leonard's.
